53% of Americans are willing to accept limits on press freedom to prevent false news

A recent report by the Pew Research Center found that many Americans are open to limits on press freedom when it comes to national security and false news.

Prasanna Bachchhav

15 September, 2026 10:11 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File photo of US President Donald Trump | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: A majority of Americans value press freedom, but a significant number of them are open to some limits on it if doing so curbs inaccurate reporting, states a recent report by the Pew Research Center. While 73 per cent of the survey respondents said that they considered press freedom to be very important to the well-being of society, about 53 per cent maintained that some constraints are acceptable in matters of national security and false information.

“(Press freedom is) designed to protect all of us. It’s a point of pride of this country,” said a Left-leaning man in his 60s. “And that’s not true in a lot of other countries. … It’s for the benefit to the country and its citizens, even more than the journalists.”

Democrats (81 per cent) are more likely than Republicans (66 per cent) to say that press freedom is highly important in a country.

Show Full Article

Published Tuesday, the report is based on two surveys conducted in March and June 2026. The first was conducted among 3,507 American adults, and the second considered 3,488 individuals. The Pew Research Center also conducted 10 online focus group discussions with 74 participants, held between May and June 2026.

Trump 2.0 and press freedom Overall, 44 per cent of Americans said the press has become less free during the second Trump administration, compared with 12 per cent who said it has become more free. About 26 per cent held that there has been no change, and 17 per cent couldn’t be sure.

“I think the powers that be in this country don’t care as much about the Constitution as the rest of us,” a Left-leaning man in his 50s said. “They will try to limit everything that they can that doesn’t slant their way or make them look good. That’s a real big problem for me.”

One in five Republicans said the press has become more free during the second Trump administration. In focus groups, several Right-leaning participants supported Elon Musk’s purchase of Twitter (now X). A man in his 50s called it “a big turning point”.

Those on the Right point to the Biden administration’s reluctance to engage with the media when questioned about Trump.

“I like the fact that President Trump, at least he knows how to hold a press conference every week, versus the administration before,” said a Right-leaning man in his 60s. “We got nothing.”

Europeans are losing purchasing power by keeping money in banks, says study

The study, conducted by financial technology company Revolut, is based on a survey of 20,007 adults across 20 EU member states along with official deposit and inflation data.

Saman Husain

15 September, 2026 07:15 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

FILE PHOTO: European Union flags flutter outside the European Commission headquarters, on the day of a European Union leaders' summit in Brussels, Belgium, December 18, 2025. | REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq/File Photo

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Europeans are losing an average of €294 in purchasing power for every €10,000 they keep in their bank instead of investing, according to a study by financial technology company Revolut.

The company’s European Wealth Drain Index, published last week, found that nearly €6.3 trillion was held in low-yield deposits. This had been found after 20 European Union countries were covered by its research.

The study is based on a survey of 20,007 adults across these 20 member states along with official deposit and inflation data. It found that average one-year deposit rates stood at 2.76 per cent, compared with inflation of 2.94 per cent.

Show Full Article

In 12 of the 20 markets surveyed, average deposit rates failed to keep pace with inflation. This means that savers were losing purchasing power even when their money was locked away for a year.

Revolut said the opportunity cost was considerably higher when compared with investments. Using the MSCI Europe ETF’s 10-year annualised return of 9.06 per cent as a benchmark, it was calculated that households forgo an average of €638 per €10,000 each year by keeping their money in cash.

Across the €6.3 trillion in deposits covered by the study, that would amount to €422 billion a year in potential growth capital that does not reach European businesses, according to Revolut.

The study has identified inertia, lack of awareness, and fragmented financial services as some of the reasons Europeans continue to hold onto their cash.

Two-thirds of respondents said they had never switched banks for a better rate. Among them, 26 per cent said they preferred their existing bank, 18 per cent considered the difference in rates negligible, and 15 per cent did not know where to look.

Close to half, or 46 per cent, incorrectly assessed their returns after inflation, while 19 per cent were unaware that inflation affected the value of their cash. One in five Europeans said they had no savings at all.

Among those who do not invest, 29 per cent cited perceived risk as the main barrier and 27 per cent pointed to a lack of knowledge.

Rolandas Juteika, Revolut’s head of wealth and trading, told Euronews that automatic investment enrollment would not address the underlying causes of this inertia.

He said Revolut’s median first-time investment in the EU was €18, arguing that lowering the barrier to entry could encourage consumers to start investing.

Also read: Deepfake porn targets EU women politicians 33 times more than men, study finds

An investment crunch The findings come as the European Union seeks to channel more household savings into capital markets through its Savings and Investments Union.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen had said last month that €10 trillion in household savings were held in bank accounts and argued that Europe needed to put more of those savings to work for European companies.

The Commission figure differs from Revolut’s €6.3 trillion estimate because it covers household savings held in bank accounts across the entire EU, while Revolut’s figure covers only the liquid deposits in 20 member states.

The European Commission has said that the Savings and Investments Union could unlock up to €470 billion in additional investment.

The push comes as Europe faces significant investment needs. The Draghi report has estimated that the bloc would require an additional €750 billion to €800 billion in investment each year by 2030 for areas including digitalisation, energy, defence, and infrastructure.

(Edited by Aamaan Alam Khan)

Modi raised India’s concerns with Xi, told Chinese President ‘3 mutuals’ should guide ties: MEA

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi also said the two leaders ‘agreed to jointly maintain peace and tranquility in border areas’ during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit.

Keshav Padmanabhan

15 September, 2026 07:01 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Chinese President Xi Jinping at Bharat Mandapam during the BRICS Summit in New Delhi | REUTERS

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi underlined that India-China relations should be guided by mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity to each other’s core concerns during his bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Tuesday.

Speaking at a press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said “several issues” were discussed during the meeting held on Saturday on the sidelines of the BRICS Leaders’ Summit. The Chinese readout on the meeting also highlighted that India’s position on Taiwan and Tibet “remain unchanged”.

“On the mentioning of certain issues in the Chinese declaration, I will say that several issues came up during the discussions, and we have kept you updated on those. The Prime Minister referred to Indian concerns and underlined that both sides should show sensitivity to each other’s core concerns and be guided by the three mutuals – mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity,” Jaiswal said when asked about the Chinese readout.

Show Full Article

Xi’s visit to India for the BRICS Summit marked his first in seven years and his first since the two militaries clashed in Eastern Ladakh in 2020.

During the meeting, Modi underlined that “peace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations”. Both leaders affirmed that “ differences should not become disputes ”.

The 2020 clashes had triggered a political chill in ties, with India maintaining that other discussions could not proceed until peace returned to the affected areas along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

In October 2024, India announced an agreement with China to disengage from the friction points along the LAC, paving the way for a calibrated thaw in ties.

The two countries have since resumed direct flights, while New Delhi has eased visa and business restrictions on Chinese nationals. Beijing resumed the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra in 2025 and held a second pilgrimage this summer.

“Xi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted a candid and in-depth exchange of views on strategic, long-term and directional issues concerning China-India relations,” Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi was reported as saying by state news agency Xinhua on Sunday. He said the most important consensus reached was that China and India should be partners.

Wang added that the two leaders “agreed to jointly maintain peace and tranquility in the border areas”. India has also offered support to Beijing for its BRICS chairship in 2027.

The thaw has extended to economic ties, with India easing some restrictions on Chinese investment imposed after the Galwan clashes. In March, the Union government eased certain investment restrictions on countries sharing a land border with India in select sectors.

India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval travelled to Beijing last month for talks with Wang under the Special Representative mechanism. The talks highlighted efforts towards an “early harvest” agreement between the two countries to demarcate the boundary in areas where there are no differences. The two sides also agreed to finalise terms of reference for two new expert groups under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC).

Days before Xi’s arrival in India, the two militaries held a corps commander-level meeting in the Eastern Sector for the first time. The meeting was part of broader efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to maintain peace along the border.

(Edited by Chingkheinganbi Mayengbam)

NATO jets shoot down ‘unidentified’ drone that entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus

The drone was intercepted near Kruonis hydroelectric power plant. In previous months, similar incidents were also registered in Latvia and Estonia.

Milda Seputyte

15 September, 2026 01:57 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Italian Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jets. Photographer: | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

NATO jets shot down an unidentified drone that flew into the Lithuanian airspace from neighboring Belarus early Tuesday, the latest incursion on the alliance’s eastern flank as aerial warfare between Ukraine and Russia intensifies.

The drone was intercepted over Pratkunai in central Lithuania, the area close to a hydroelectric power plant of Kruonis, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said. Air alerts sounded out over the capital region of Vilnius and the country’s second-largest city Kaunas before the drone was brought down.

It was the first time that NATO shot down a drone over the territory of Lithuania. The incident follows similar incidents in neighboring Latvia and Estonia in recent months. Intensifying exchanges of air attacks between Ukraine and Russia are turning into a growing issue for NATO countries as drones are jammed or veer off course.

Show Full Article

“Even though the war seems to be taking place a thousand kilometers away from Lithuania, its scale is still large and extensive,” Kaunas told national broadcaster LRT Tuesday. “Russia’s unwillingness to come to peace negotiations affects the security of the Baltic region.”

NATO jets downed a drone over Latvia in August after it entered the country’s airspace as a result of Russian electronic warfare, and a Romanian F-16 shot down a suspected Ukrainian drone over Estonia in May. Poland said Monday that the Polish military retrieved a Russian military UAV from the Baltic Sea near the town of Rusinowo.

European officials have also warned that Russia may escalate sabotage and covert attacks against the continent as it struggles to make progress in its war in Ukraine that’s now in a fifth year. Germany earlier this month attributed a drone attack on a Leipzig airport to Russian intelligence and said it expects further hybrid aggression.
